alma-mater-studiorum-universita-di-bolog.about:
The University of Bologna is a large public multi-campus university with sites in Bologna, Cesena, Forlì, Ravenna and Rimini. It is strong across economics, law, political science, medicine, engineering, agriculture and the humanities, and teaches a growing list of international first-cycle degrees in English, such as Business and Economics, Economics and Finance, and Genomics.

Each programme sets its own call for applications, admission test (SAT, TOLC, IMAT or programme-specific) and deadlines. Fees depend on family income, so many international students pay little, and the regional ER.GO agency awards need-based grants and housing.
alma-mater-studiorum-universita-di-bolog.aid_intl: Need-based ER.GO regional grants and fee exemptions open to international students; Unibo Action 1&2 study grants for international students on some programmes.
alma-mater-studiorum-universita-di-bolog.tests: Admission tests vary by programme and are set out in each call: many English-taught bachelor's accept SAT or TOLC results; medicine/dentistry in English use the IMAT. Language: proof of English (often B2) for English-taught programmes, Italian for Italian-taught ones.
alma-mater-studiorum-universita-di-bolog.gpa_note: Selection usually combines school grades with the admission test score set in each programme's call.
requirements: Secondary school transcripts
School-leaving diploma (12 years of schooling) with Declaration of Value/CIMEA statement if required
Admission test per programme call (e.g. SAT, TOLC or IMAT)
English proficiency for English-taught programmes (often B2)
Passport
Universitaly pre-enrolment (non-EU students needing a visa)
ISEE or foreign income documents for fee reductions

erasmus-university-rotterdam.about:
Erasmus University Rotterdam is a specialised research university focused on business, economics, law, medicine, social sciences, history and philosophy. Its Rotterdam School of Management (RSM) and Erasmus School of Economics are among Europe's best known, and the Erasmus MC medical centre is one of the largest in the Netherlands.

International bachelor's options include International Business Administration, International Bachelor in Economics and Business Economics, econometrics, communication and media, psychology and liberal arts at Erasmus University College. Numerus fixus programmes require Studielink registration by 15 January and select by grades and motivation.
erasmus-university-rotterdam.aid_intl: Limited merit scholarships for non-EEA students (e.g. Holland Scholarship and Erasmus-specific awards).
erasmus-university-rotterdam.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement in general. English and mathematics minimums depend on your diploma type and are listed per programme. Numerus fixus programmes (e.g. IBA, 650 places) rank applicants by grades (75%) and motivation.
top_programs: International Bachelor Economics and Business Economics
Liberal Arts and Sciences (Erasmus University College)
erasmus-university-rotterdam.gpa_note: For IBA, grades count 75% of selection points; high averages and strong maths are needed.
requirements: Secondary school transcripts
Secondary school diploma (meeting the programme's diploma requirements)
English proficiency as required for your diploma type
Motivation questions in the programme application
Studielink registration and programme online application form
Passport

rmit-university.about:
RMIT (Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology) is a dual-sector public university with a city campus woven into Melbourne's CBD, plus campuses in Vietnam and a presence in Spain. It is internationally known for art and design, architecture, communication and media, and also offers engineering, IT, aviation, business and health degrees with a strong emphasis on industry projects and work-integrated learning.

International students apply online directly or through an agent, meeting course-specific academic and English requirements; creative programmes may require a folio. Semester 1 starts in March and Semester 2 in July, and merit scholarships are available for many regions.
rmit-university.aid_intl: Merit scholarships for international students, including regional Academic Merit Scholarships and joint scholarships with national funding bodies (e.g. Colfuturo, China Scholarship Council).
rmit-university.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement in general; entry is by secondary qualification against course minimums. English: course-specific IELTS (Academic) or equivalent, listed on each course page. Some design and media courses require a folio or selection task.
rmit-university.gpa_note: Course-specific minimums for your qualification; design courses also weigh the folio.
requirements: Secondary school results (final or predicted)
Secondary school completion certificate
English test meeting the course's IELTS level
Folio or selection task for some design/media courses
Passport
Proof of funds for the Australian student visa

university-of-north-carolina-at-chapel-h.about:
Chartered in 1789, UNC-Chapel Hill is the flagship of the University of North Carolina system, set in a classic college town within the Research Triangle. It is renowned for its Gillings School of Global Public Health, Kenan-Flagler Business School, Hussman School of Journalism and Media, and strong sciences, and North Carolina law caps out-of-state students at a small share of each class.

International students apply via the Common App with essays, a counselor recommendation and English test results; SAT/ACT are optional for most. Internationals are not eligible for need-based aid and must budget for the full non-resident cost, but a handful of merit scholarships (such as Morehead-Cain) are open to them.
university-of-north-carolina-at-chapel-h.aid_intl: No need-based aid for students without US citizenship or permanent residency; a few merit scholarships are open to all applicants.
university-of-north-carolina-at-chapel-h.tests: SAT/ACT optional for applicants with a weighted GPA of 2.8+ (otherwise SAT 930+/ACT 17+ required). Middle 50% of enrolled first-years (CDS 2025-26): SAT 1400–1530, ACT 29–34. English proficiency: TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Cambridge C1/C2 accepted (waivable after four years in an English-speaking country); no minimum published.
university-of-north-carolina-at-chapel-h.gpa_note: Most admitted students are at the very top of their class with rigorous coursework (AP/IB/A-levels).
requirements: High school transcript
Completion of the pre-university curriculum (e.g. A-levels, Baccalaureate)
Common App essay and UNC short-answer questions
Counselor recommendation (teacher recommendation optional)
English proficiency test (TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo/Cambridge)
SAT/ACT optional with weighted GPA 2.8+
Application fee ($85) or waiver
Proof of funds for the F-1 visa after admission

university-of-oslo.about:
Founded in 1811, the University of Oslo is Norway's leading research university, with its main Blindern campus and a historic law faculty in central Oslo. It has eight faculties spanning law, humanities, social sciences, mathematics and natural sciences, medicine, dentistry, education and theology.

For international undergraduates the options are narrow: one English-taught bachelor's programme, while all other bachelor's degrees require Norwegian. Since 2023 students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland pay tuition, and UiO offers no degree scholarships, though the master's level has many more English-taught programmes.
university-of-oslo.aid_intl: None: UiO does not offer scholarships for full bachelor's or master's degree students.
university-of-oslo.tests: No SAT/ACT. Norwegian-taught bachelor's require proof of Norwegian proficiency (UiO offers no preparatory Norwegian courses before admission). The English-taught bachelor's requires English proficiency as set in its admission rules.
university-of-oslo.gpa_note: Competitive programmes rank applicants by school grade points (converted for foreign qualifications).
requirements: Secondary school transcripts
Secondary school diploma meeting Norwegian general entrance requirements
English proficiency (English-taught programme) or Norwegian proficiency (Norwegian-taught)
Passport
Proof of funds for the residence permit (NOK 170,368 for 2026/27) and tuition

university-of-vienna.about:
The University of Vienna is Austria's largest university, with around 90,000 students spread across historic buildings in central Vienna. It covers nearly every academic field, from philosophy, history and linguistics to physics, mathematics, life sciences, psychology, business and law, with a strong research profile in the humanities and natural sciences.

International bachelor's applicants apply online in the semester's application period, have their school-leaving certificate checked for equivalence, and must reach German C1 before enrolment (A2 is enough to apply). Fees are very low by international standards, though student-visa holders must show proof of funds.
university-of-vienna.aid_intl: No general university scholarships for full degree students from abroad; some external grants (e.g. OeAD) and fee waivers for certain countries.
university-of-vienna.tests: No SAT/ACT. Almost all bachelor's programmes are taught in German: you can apply with German at A2 level, but need C1 German before you can enrol (the university's preparatory programme can bridge the gap). A few programmes require English proficiency. Some subjects (e.g. psychology, business, computer science, education) have entrance exams/aptitude tests.
university-of-vienna.gpa_note: Admission is open to holders of an equivalent university entrance qualification; restricted subjects select via entrance exams.
requirements: School-leaving certificate and transcripts (legalised/translated if required)
Proof of general university entrance qualification (country-specific requirements)
German A2 to apply, C1 before enrolment (English for English-taught programmes)
Passport
Entrance exam/aptitude test for restricted programmes
Proof of funds for the Austrian residence permit

western-university.about:
Western University is one of Canada's leading research universities, with a large, traditional campus in London, Ontario, guaranteed first-year residence and a strong student culture. It has 11 faculties and is best known for the Ivey Business School's HBA programme, medicine and health sciences, engineering, media studies and music.

International students apply through OUAC, are assessed on their high-school grades (SAT/ACT not required) and English proficiency (IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 83 / Duolingo 115), and are considered for entrance and national scholarships. Many students pursue Ivey through Advanced Entry Opportunity status from first year.
western-university.aid_intl: Merit scholarships for international students, including Western's National Scholarships and entrance awards; no need-based aid for most internationals.
western-university.tests: SAT/ACT not required; international high-school curricula are assessed on grades (AP/IB considered). English for Fall 2027 (tests taken from 1 Jan 2025, before March 2027): IELTS Academic 6.5 with 6.0 in each section; TOEFL iBT 83 with 20 in each section; Duolingo 115. Lower scores can qualify for the English Boost Program.
western-university.gpa_note: Competitive high-school grades required; most programmes admit in the high-80s % range equivalent and above.
requirements: High school transcripts
Secondary school diploma
English test (IELTS 6.5, 6.0 per section / TOEFL iBT 83, 20 per section / Duolingo 115)
Ivey AEO application or programme supplements where required
OUAC application fee
Passport
Proof of funds for the Canadian study permit
